sections.h2: Where is a Jessamine County deed recorded?
sections.html:
A deed for land in Jessamine County is recorded with the Jessamine County Clerk in Nicholasville. The clerk's main office is in the courthouse at 101 North Main Street, open Monday through Friday from 8 AM to 4 PM, and the real estate line is (859) 885-4161.

There is also a Wilmore branch at 210 South Lexington Avenue, open Monday through Friday from 9 AM to 3 PM, according to the county's own listing. Call ahead before you drive there with a closing package, because the county page does not say which services each office handles. Nicholasville is both the county seat and the largest city, so most sellers deal with the downtown courthouse.

Selling a house here usually ends with a deed, a release of the old mortgage, and sometimes an affidavit. All three land in the same set of land records, and a buyer's title agent will want to see each one indexed before funding is final.

Plan the visit around three items:

  • The deed itself, with the value or consideration stated, since the transfer tax is figured from it.
  • Payment for the recording fee and the transfer tax. KRS 64.012 also sets a $5 fee if the clerk notarizes or acknowledges the deed on the spot.
  • The release for the seller's old mortgage, if the lender has not recorded it already. The posted minimum for a release is $46. The county also posts an open records request form on its clerk page for anyone who needs copies later.

sections.h2: What does the Jessamine County Clerk charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
The clerk's posted schedule lists $50 as the minimum for a deed and $80 for a mortgage. That schedule shows an effective date of January 1, 2020, so ask the clerk's office for the current total before you bring a check.

Sample minimum recording fees on the Jessamine County Clerk schedule
DocumentPosted minimum
Deed or condominium deed$50
Mortgage$80
Release of mortgage, full or partial$46
Affidavit of descent$50
Power of attorney$50
Easement$50
Plat$50
Will$47

Source: Jessamine County Clerk, Standard Recording Fees page.

Most items add $3 for every page past the first five, and a mortgage adds $3 for every page past thirty. The base figure in the statute, KRS 64.012, is $33 for a recorded instrument of up to five pages, so the clerk's posted minimums include more than that one line. Treat the posted number as a floor.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax applies when a Jessamine County house sells?
sections.html:
Kentucky charges the seller 50 cents for each $500 of value in the deed, and a fraction of $500 counts as a full unit. The Jessamine County Clerk collects it when the deed is presented, because a deed cannot be recorded until the tax is paid.

Here is a worked example using the county's Census median owner-occupied value of $268,100. That figure divides into 537 units of $500 once the fraction is rounded up, so the tax comes to $268.50. A $400,000 sale would produce $400.00. The tax is paid once per sale, in the county where the property sits.

The statute at KRS 142.050 lists transfers that owe nothing. These are the ones sellers ask about most:

  • Transfers between spouses, or between former spouses as part of a divorce.
  • A deed between parent and child, or grandparent and grandchild, for only nominal consideration.
  • A deed that confirms or corrects one already recorded.
  • A transfer under foreclosure, or a voluntary surrender in place of foreclosure.
  • A deed given only to provide or release security for a debt.

For a gift or a deed with token consideration, the clerk looks to the estimated open market price when an exemption does not apply.

sections.h2: Can I search or e-record Jessamine County land records online?
sections.html:
Yes. The clerk offers eCCLIX, a subscription service for viewing and printing indexed documents, and it accepts e-recording through four named vendors. Anyone can view the records for free in the office itself.

The clerk's records page says deeds, mortgages and wills are indexed back to June 30, 1966, and online images cover most instruments from January 2004 forward. Marriage records go back to 1798. If you are tracing an old boundary or a lien from decades ago, the in-person index is the better starting point.

  • eCCLIX: account and password issued by the site administrator, with access fees charged for data and images.
  • Indecomm: (704) 412-3179.
  • CSC: (866) 652-0111.
  • Simplifile: (800) 460-5657.
  • ePN: (888) 325-3365.

The clerk also offers DOCALERT, a free service that emails you when a deed or mortgage is filed under your name. Owners of inherited or vacant property in Jessamine County should consider signing up, since a forged deed is easier to catch the week it is filed than a year later.

sections.h2: What happens with property tax after a Jessamine County deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The Jessamine County Property Valuation Administrator tracks deed transfers and updates the owner of record, while the sheriff bills and collects the tax. The clerk is involved again only when a bill goes unpaid.

The PVA says the homestead exemption for owners 65 and older follows the person and not the house. A seller who receives it should tell the PVA office about the move so the exemption comes off the old address. The PVA's announcement for 2025 to 2026 lists the exemption at $49,100.

Bills not paid by April 15 are sent from the sheriff to the county clerk, and the clerk's website carries a delinquent tax search. The state Department of Revenue says interest of 1 percent per month and added fees begin once the clerk holds the bill, so a seller with an old unpaid bill should clear it before the deed is signed. Ask the clerk for the exact payoff figure before closing.

sections.h2: What should a Jessamine County seller know about the local housing base?
sections.html:
Jessamine County is growing quickly for a Kentucky county its size. The Census Bureau counted 52,991 residents in 2020 and estimated 57,147 for July 2025, a gain of 7.8 percent, in a county of about 172 square miles of land.

The county was cut from Fayette County land in December 1798, and the clerk says some records date back to the 1700s. The county sits in the Lexington-Fayette metro area and the Kentucky River forms its entire southern border. Nicholasville and Wilmore are the two incorporated cities, with High Bridge a census-designated place. Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show 66.7 percent of homes owner-occupied, a median household income of $74,576, and 512 building permits issued in 2025.

That mix of new construction and long-held farmland keeps title work busy. Parcels split from farms often come with easements, plats and survey references, and each of those is a separate recorded item at the clerk's counter.

faqs.q: Who records deeds in Jessamine County, Kentucky?
faqs.a: The Jessamine County Clerk records them. The main office is at 101 North Main Street in Nicholasville and the real estate phone line is (859) 885-4161.

faqs.q: Is the Jessamine County recording fee the same as the one in state law?
faqs.a: No. KRS 64.012 sets $33 for a recorded instrument of up to five pages, while the clerk's posted minimum for a deed is $50. Ask the clerk for the current total.

faqs.q: Does the seller or the buyer pay Kentucky transfer tax?
faqs.a: The statute puts it on the grantor named in the deed, which is the seller. It is 50 cents per $500 of value, collected by the clerk at recording.

faqs.q: Can I get notified if someone files a deed in my name?
faqs.a: Yes. The Jessamine County Clerk offers DOCALERT, a free email alert for any deed or mortgage recorded under your name or business name.

faqs.q: Where do I look up an old deed in Jessamine County?
faqs.a: Use the indexes at the clerk's office, which are free to view in person, or subscribe to eCCLIX. Deeds are indexed back to June 30, 1966.
